significance: Varanasi's celebrated leaning temple, standing at the foot of Manikarnika Ghat with a tilt of about nine degrees and its sanctum flooded for much of the year. Revenue records date it to 1825-30, though its patron is disputed between a servant of Raja Man Singh, the Amethi royal house, Baija Bai of Gwalior and Ratna Bai, a servant of Ahilya Bai of Indore.
story: One account holds that Ahilya Bai cursed the temple to lean because her servant Ratna Bai had named it after herself.
